title: procurement-tools part-number equivalence record
description: One product family across regions, brands and channels: which part numbers name the same object, which are near-siblings that differ in a way that matters, and which are the traps that look like the right part and are not. Written by the part-number-equivalence skill to data/equivalence/<family>.json.

anchor.description: The part number the search started from — usually the one the user found.

naming_scheme.description: How this manufacturer builds its part numbers, once decoded — which segment is the range, which is the feature suffix, which is the regional unit system. This is the reusable finding; it usually generalises to the manufacturer's whole catalogue.

region.description: ISO country/region code, or a market name like 'EU', 'NA', 'MEA'.

brand.description: Where the same object is sold under another brand — OEM, private label, or a licensed regional brand.

relation.description: decoy = a part number that looks like the anchor and is materially different. Recording it is often the most valuable row in the file.

differences.description: Required for anything that is not 'identical'. What actually differs: units, mains plug, radio certification, bundled accessories, firmware, warranty region.

spec_impact.description: Whether any difference touches a requirement in the spec, and which one.

confidence.description: confirmed requires a source that states the link — a manufacturer cross-reference, a shared declaration of conformity, matching datasheets under both numbers. Two retailers saying so is 'probable' at best.

buy_implications.description: What the equivalence means for the actual purchase: which number to search in which market, what a cheaper sibling costs you, what will not be honoured under warranty when imported.
